rituals.title: THE SECURE PENDING BOX
rituals.goal: Unfinished material needs a boundary, not denial.
rituals.steps:
1. Imagine Container — Imagine a container whose lock, size, material, and location feel credible.
2. Place Cannot — Place only what cannot be processed now inside it.
3. Name Stored — Name what is stored and when it will be revisited, ideally with support.
4. Close Container — Close the container and reorient to the next task for today.
rituals.win: ✓ Someone else’s share moved back out of my hands.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Close Container”; orient to now.
• Use “Name Stored” on return.
• “Name Stored” moves memory toward then.
• What lost power: “Imagine Container” → “Close Container”?
• I can use “Place Cannot” while staying in now.
rituals.formula_flow: Imagine Container → Place Cannot → Name Stored → Close Container
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use containment to postpone urgent safeguarding or necessary care.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: BUILD SAFE-ENOUGH, NOT PERFECT
rituals.goal: A believable refuge works better than fantasy pressure.
rituals.steps:
1. Place Five — Picture a place using five sensory facts and one control feature: an exit, boundary, companion, or adjustable distance.
2. Rehearse Specific — practise entering through a specific cue and leaving on purpose.
3. Strengthen Safe-Enough — Strengthen the detail that produces the clearest bodily yes.
rituals.win: ✓ Progress no longer has to audition as perfection.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Strengthen Safe-Enough”; orient to now.
• If it flares, choose “Rehearse Specific”.
• “Rehearse Specific” moves memory toward then.
• Difference check: “Place Five” → “Strengthen Safe-Enough”.
• I can use “Rehearse Specific” while staying in now.
rituals.formula_flow: Place Five → Rehearse Specific → Strengthen Safe-Enough
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Abandon imagery that attracts threat memories or increases unreality.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: ONE-WORD LIGHT TOUCH
rituals.goal: Name enough to see; not enough to build a story.
rituals.steps:
1. Apply Quiet — As events arise, apply a quiet category: hearing, planning, heat, remembering, pressure.
2. Use Word — Use one word once, then return to the raw event.
3. Name Lightly — If a label starts producing analysis, name that ‘explaining’ and release it.
rituals.win: ✓ One word was enough; explanation did not get a sequel.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Name Lightly”; keep the compass.
• On return: “Use Word”.
• “Use Word” keeps meaning in motion.
• Look back: “Apply Quiet” → “Name Lightly”.
• I can use “Use Word” while pain stays real.
rituals.formula_flow: Apply Quiet → Use Word → Name Lightly
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Drop noting if labels become compulsive, critical, or distancing.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: CLOSE THE MICRO-GAPS
rituals.goal: Meditative flow is repaired one break at a time.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose Precise — Choose an anchor and notice the precise moment contact breaks.
2. Return Instead — Instead of judging the distraction, shorten the delay before returning.
3. Track Interval — Track the interval between noticing and reconnection.
4. Let Practice — Let practice end after one stretch with visibly fewer or shorter gaps.
rituals.win: ✓ The practice has fewer leaks than it did a minute ago.
rituals.supports:
• One exhale after “Let Practice”; redirect attention.
• Loop back? Use “Track Interval”.
• “Track Interval” proves one signal leads.
• Difference check: “Choose Precise” → “Let Practice”.
• I can use “Return Instead” amid noise.
rituals.formula_flow: Choose Precise → Return Instead → Track Interval → Let Practice
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Release focus if effort becomes rigid, painful, or compulsive.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: BREAK THE NIGHT'S STORYLINE
rituals.goal: Sleep does not need another storyline to solve.
rituals.steps:
1. Pick Word — Choose one harmless five-letter word, such as TABLE. Use each letter once; there is no need to finish perfectly.
2. Call Object — For the first letter, name a neutral object beginning with it—T for tree, for example.
3. Flash Image — Picture that object for about two seconds with no action, meaning, memory, or story.
4. Jump Letter — Jump to the next letter and a completely unrelated object. End after five letters; do not score sleep.
rituals.win: ✓ I ended after five letters; do not score sleep.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Jump Letter”; loosen the label.
• Skip replay; use “Flash Image”.
• “Flash Image” — the rule loosened.
• What lost power: “Pick Word” → “Jump Letter”?
• I can use “Call Object” without becoming the label.
rituals.formula_flow: Pick Word → Call Object → Flash Image → Jump Letter
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use only while safely resting; never while driving. Stop if images become distressing, compulsive, or disorienting.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE ACTION HAD MANY AUTHORS
rituals.goal: Total doership omits most of the production team.
rituals.steps:
1. Name Conditions — Review one action and name its conditions: intention, habit, body capacity, other people, tools, timing, culture, and chance.
2. Place Yourself — Place yourself among these causes rather than above them.
3. Keep Responsibility — Keep responsibility for your contribution while releasing sole authorship.
rituals.win: ✓ Body noise no longer gets to write the conclusion alone.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Keep Responsibility”; no forcing.
• Re-entry move: “Place Yourself”.
• “Place Yourself” keeps sensation as data.
• Compare “Name Conditions” with “Keep Responsibility”.
• I can use “Place Yourself” while sensation stays.
rituals.formula_flow: Name Conditions → Place Yourself → Keep Responsibility
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not scattered accountability for choices that caused harm.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: MAKE THE FIRST MOVE DELIBERATELY WRONG
rituals.goal: A throwaway mistake can make the first move lose its authority.
rituals.steps:
1. Throwaway — Open a private mental sandbox and mark it THROWAWAY—NOT FOR SENDING.
2. Make Wrong — Imagine one obviously imperfect start: a clumsy first sentence, rough title, messy mental sketch, or unfinished opening.
3. Fix One — Correct exactly one useful part without polishing the rest.
4. Continue Clean — Keep working only if the task now feels editable; otherwise keep the corrected fragment in mind and stop cleanly.
rituals.win: ✓ The work can move without earning a flawless score first.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Continue Clean”; release the score.
• Skip replay; use “Fix One”.
• “Fix One” keeps progress moving imperfectly.
• “Continue Clean”: what changed from “Throwaway”?
• I can use “Make Wrong” without perfecting.
rituals.formula_flow: Throwaway → Make Wrong → Fix One → Continue Clean
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Never use deliberate errors in medical, legal, financial, safety-critical, submitted, or live shared work.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: ALLY OR SABOTEUR?
rituals.goal: Judge the mental move by how it treats your life.
rituals.steps:
1. Ask Thought — Ask the current thought three questions: Does it clarify the next move?
2. Check Protection — Does it protect something real?
3. Leave Me — Does it leave me more capable afterward?
4. Score Yes — Score each yes or no.
5. Thank Warning — If it fails two, thank the warning and appoint a different inner adviser.
rituals.win: ✓ Kept the warning, fired the sabotage, and chose a better adviser.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Thank Warning”; slow the clock.
• Return once to “Leave Me”.
• “Score Yes” puts facts above speed.
• What lost power: “Ask Thought” → “Thank Warning”?
• I can use “Check Protection” without rushing.
rituals.formula_flow: Ask Thought → Check Protection → Leave Me → Score Yes → Thank Warning
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
A harsh message may still contain facts; extract them before dismissal.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: STOP RENEWING THE CONSTRUCTION
rituals.goal: Some mental worlds persist through continuous subscription.
rituals.steps:
1. Identify Image — Spot the image, conclusion, or demand being refreshed.
2. Time — For one minute, refuse only the renewal: no new scene, argument, or confirmation.
3. Let Existing — Let existing residue fade at its own rate.
4. Redirect — Redirect the freed attention into a chosen sensory task.
rituals.win: ✓ The construction crew clocked off; attention returned to the real room.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Redirect”; notice the room.
• Loop back? Use “Let Existing”.
• “Let Existing” proves the present returned.
• “Identify Image” to “Redirect”: what loosened?
• I can use “Time” to return here.
rituals.formula_flow: Identify Image → Time → Let Existing → Redirect
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not withdraw intention from real obligations or safety planning.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: PRECISE OUTSIDE, QUIET INSIDE
rituals.goal: Action can be sharp without inner warfare.
rituals.steps:
1. Define — Set the exact external behaviour required.
2. Execute — Execute it with full timing and skill.
3. Imagine Applause — Meanwhile, decline the running argument about authorship, resentment, or imagined applause.
4. Let Body — Allow the body act and the inner courtroom remain closed until the task ends.
rituals.win: ✓ The action stayed precise while the inner courtroom stayed closed.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Let Body”; no forcing.
• Shortcut: “Imagine Applause”, once.
• “Imagine Applause” keeps sensation as data.
• Difference check: “Define” → “Let Body”.
• I can use “Execute” while sensation stays.
rituals.formula_flow: Define → Execute → Imagine Applause → Let Body
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Process emotions later if quieting argument would become suppression.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: NEXT PHYSICAL MOVEMENT
rituals.goal: Projects become executable when nouns turn into verbs.
rituals.steps:
1. Take Stuck — Take the stuck item and ask what your body would visibly do first: open, call, search, carry, type, ask, measure.
2. Include Object — Include the object and location.
3. Plan Remainder — do that movement before planning the remainder.
rituals.win: ✓ Planning shrank to one physical move.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Plan Remainder”; no breath-holding.
• Catch restart with “Include Object”.
• “Include Object” — alarm isn’t command.
• Before/after: “Take Stuck” → “Plan Remainder”.
• I can use “Include Object” while alarm rises.
rituals.formula_flow: Take Stuck → Include Object → Plan Remainder
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Check dependencies first when the movement could create hard to undo consequences.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: SOFT DELIVERY, SOLID MESSAGE
rituals.goal: Relationship care does not require surrendering the point.
rituals.steps:
1. Remove Attacks — Remove attacks from your wording.
2. Validate Understandable — Show one sign of genuine interest, validate the understandable part of the other experience, and use an easy rather than contemptuous manner.
3. Keep Core — Keep your core message unchanged.
4. Edit Delivery — Gentleness edits delivery, not truth.
rituals.win: ✓ I softened the delivery without softening the message.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Edit Delivery”; soften the jaw.
• Loop back? Use “Keep Core”.
• “Keep Core” keeps clarity above heat.
• “Remove Attacks” → “Edit Delivery”: what changed?
• I can use “Validate Understandable” without extra heat.
rituals.formula_flow: Remove Attacks → Validate Understandable → Keep Core → Edit Delivery
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not prioritise pleasantness over protection in abusive dynamics.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: SELF-RESPECT CHECKSUM
rituals.goal: A conversation should not corrupt your own values.
rituals.steps:
1. Respond Verify — Before responding, verify four conditions: fair to both sides; no apology for merely existing or setting a limit; aligned with your values; completely truthful.
2. Revise Sentence — Revise any sentence that fails the checksum.
3. Speak Cleanly — Then speak without extra justification.
rituals.win: ✓ Message delivered cleanly—no extra defence added.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Speak Cleanly”; keep the compass.
• Shortcut: “Revise Sentence”, once.
• “Revise Sentence” keeps meaning in motion.
• At “Speak Cleanly”, compare “Respond Verify”.
• I can use “Revise Sentence” while pain stays real.
rituals.formula_flow: Respond Verify → Revise Sentence → Speak Cleanly
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Fairness does not require equal power where harm or coercion exists.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: VALIDATE AT THE DEPTH YOU ACTUALLY HAVE
rituals.goal: Understanding has levels; do not counterfeit the deepest one.
rituals.steps:
1. Start Attention — Start with attention. Reflect what you heard.
2. Name Emotion — Identify the emotion if clear.
3. Add Context — Include context that makes the response understandable.
4. Acknowledge — Acknowledge valid facts.
5. Stop Highest — Stop at the highest honest rung.
rituals.win: ✓ Honesty stopped at the rung it could truly reach.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Stop Highest”; let wanting crest.
• Skip replay; use “Add Context”.
• “Acknowledge” keeps wanting off controls.
• “Start Attention” to “Stop Highest”: what loosened?
• I can use “Name Emotion” without obeying the urge.
rituals.formula_flow: Start Attention → Name Emotion → Add Context → Acknowledge → Stop Highest
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Validation should not endorse abuse, delusion, or dangerous conduct.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE FOUR-PART LIMIT
rituals.goal: A boundary becomes real when follow-through is inside your control.
rituals.steps:
1. State Triggering — State the triggering condition, your limit, the action you will take, and when you will take it.
2. Remove Threats — Remove threats that depend on the other person changing.
3. Practise Line — Practise the line once at speaking volume, then prepare the consequence before delivery.
rituals.win: ✓ My boundary now includes the part I can actually enforce.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Practise Line”; release extra load.
• Re-entry move: “Remove Threats”.
• “Remove Threats” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• “State Triggering” → “Practise Line”: what changed?
• I can use “Remove Threats” without carrying it all.
rituals.formula_flow: State Triggering → Remove Threats → Practise Line
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Seek safety planning before setting boundaries with a violent or controlling person.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: CARE WITHOUT CARRYING
rituals.goal: Empathy can cross a boundary; obligation must show its passport.
rituals.steps:
1. Separate Feelings — Name the other person’s feeling and your own current feeling separately.
2. Locate Relative — Locate each relative to your body.
3. Ask Compassionate — Ask what compassionate action is actually yours and what emotional work remains theirs.
4. Care Without Carrying — Offer the first without absorbing the second.
rituals.win: ✓ The boundary became visible without turning cold.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Care Without Carrying”; release extra load.
• Pulled back? Touch “Ask Compassionate”.
• “Ask Compassionate” keeps responsibility proportionate.
• Look back: “Separate Feelings” → “Care Without Carrying”.
• I can use “Locate Relative” without carrying it all.
rituals.formula_flow: Separate Feelings → Locate Relative → Ask Compassionate → Care Without Carrying
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Do not use emotional separation to abandon genuine duty of care.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: SAY IT IN YOUR MIND. DO NOT SEND IT.
rituals.goal: Give the feeling space without sending it to the other person.
rituals.steps:
1. See The Person — Imagine the person in front of you.
2. Say What Happened — In your mind, say what happened, what you felt, what you needed, and what you now choose to release.
3. Do Not Edit — Let the message be honest, but do not plan harm.
4. Wait — Do not contact the person for twenty-four hours. Let the message stay only in your mind.
rituals.win: ✓ I let the message stay only in my mind.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Wait”; soften the jaw.
• Re-entry move: “Do Not Edit”.
• “Do Not Edit” keeps clarity above heat.
• At “Wait”, compare “See The Person”.
• I can use “Say What Happened” without extra heat.
rituals.formula_flow: See The Person → Say What Happened → Do Not Edit → Wait
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop and seek support if the exercise increases revenge thoughts, fear, or trauma.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE TWENTY-MINUTE TRUTH STORY
rituals.goal: A private story can help your mind make sense of an event.
rituals.steps:
1. Set A Time — Choose up to twenty minutes.
2. Tell The Story — In your mind, move through what occurred, what you felt, and what it means now.
3. Return to Now — End by naming your location, today’s date, and one caring action you can take.
4. Repeat if Useful — Try again on another day only if it helps.
rituals.win: ✓ The story got a container, an ending, and permission to stay private.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Repeat if Useful”; loosen the label.
• Use “Return to Now” on return.
• “Return to Now” — the rule loosened.
• Before/after: “Set A Time” → “Repeat if Useful”.
• I can use “Tell The Story” without becoming the label.
rituals.formula_flow: Set A Time → Tell The Story → Return to Now → Repeat if Useful
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Stop if the story harms your sleep, safety, or daily life.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: CROSS OUT THE EXPIRED FUTURE
rituals.goal: A prediction should lose influence when its decision window closes.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Prediction — Picture the prediction and the exact condition that makes it obsolete: date passed, result known, action completed, evidence changed.
2. Imagine Line — When that condition arrives, imagine a line through the prediction and picture the word EXPIRED.
3. Remove Vote — It may remain historically visible, but it receives no further vote.
rituals.win: ✓ The expired future lost its vote.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Remove Vote”; leave the forecast.
• On return: “Imagine Line”.
• “Imagine Line” — fear isn’t fate.
• Before/after: “Picture Prediction” → “Remove Vote”.
• I can use “Imagine Line” while fear stays loud.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture Prediction → Imagine Line → Remove Vote
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Reopen only when genuinely new evidence creates a new forecast.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: TURN ANTICIPATION INTO INVENTORY
rituals.goal: Body alarm earns its keep only through preparation.
rituals.steps:
1. Repeat Extract — Each time the same future scene repeats, extract one actionable item: question, document, rehearsal, route, support, or if-then link.
2. Add Checklist — Add it to a checklist.
3. Stamp Simulation — When repetition yields no new preparation, stamp the simulation PAID IN FULL and switch to execution.
rituals.win: ✓ Anticipation became inventory instead of another rehearsal.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Stamp Simulation”; then keep moving.
• Re-entry move: “Add Checklist”.
• “Add Checklist” proves motion is available.
• Before/after: “Repeat Extract” → “Stamp Simulation”.
• I can use “Add Checklist” before motivation.
rituals.formula_flow: Repeat Extract → Add Checklist → Stamp Simulation
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Keep planning active for newly emerging risks rather than silencing them.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THE LIFE RETURNED TEST
rituals.goal: Imagine receiving this ordinary day back.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture — Picture having lost access to your current life and unexpectedly waking inside it again.
2. Small — What small feature would suddenly matter—someone’s voice, a body ability, unfinished work, morning light?
3. Choose Behaviour — Choose one behaviour that honours that recovered value today, without romanticising real hardship.
rituals.win: ✓ Ordinary life regained enough value to deserve one move today.
rituals.supports:
• Gently exhale after “Choose Behaviour”; no breath-holding.
• Catch restart with “Small”.
• “Small” — alarm isn’t command.
• At “Choose Behaviour”, compare “Picture”.
• I can use “Small” while alarm rises.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture → Small → Choose Behaviour
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Avoid loss imagery if it worsens grief, trauma, or suicidal thinking.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: A NOTE FROM TOMORROW MORNING
rituals.goal: Let the consequence-bearer make one request.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Tomorrow — Imagine tomorrow-you after tonight’s urge has passed. Let them ask: ‘Please protect at least…’ Then choose one minimum: sleep, money, sobriety, dignity, preparation, or safety.
2. Date It — Mentally sign the request with tomorrow’s date.
3. Place the Contract — Bring that promise to mind exactly where the immediate choice happens.
rituals.win: ✓ Tomorrow-me got one clean favour from me today.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Place the Contract”; let wanting crest.
• On return: “Date It”.
• “Date It” keeps wanting off controls.
• “Picture Tomorrow” → “Place the Contract”: what changed?
• I can use “Date It” without obeying the urge.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture Tomorrow → Date Sign → Place Contract
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Use live support when an urge threatens serious harm or relapse.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: COOL THE WORDS, KEEP THE FACTS
rituals.goal: Language can lower heat without lowering truth.
rituals.steps:
1. Underline — Underline absolutes and inflammatory terms in your account.
2. Observe Behaviour — Exchange every one for a precise factual equivalent: ‘always’ becomes the actual frequency; ‘destroyed’ becomes the specific loss; ‘evil’ becomes the observed behaviour.
3. Read Action — Re-read and notice what action the cooler version supports.
rituals.win: ✓ The facts stayed; the heat came down.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Read Action”; then keep moving.
• If it flares, choose “Observe Behaviour”.
• “Observe Behaviour” proves motion is available.
• “Underline” versus “Read Action”: what eased?
• I can use “Observe Behaviour” before motivation.
rituals.formula_flow: Underline → Observe Behaviour → Read Action
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Retain strong moral language when accurate naming is necessary.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: LOOK FOR THE MISSING DANGER
rituals.goal: Absence becomes evidence only after prediction says what should be present.
rituals.steps:
1. Ask Sign — Ask what sign must exist right now if the feared model is correct.
2. Search Fairly — Search once, fairly.
3. Mark Absence — If it is absent, keep that absence and reduce—not erase—the model’s weight.
4. Name Explanation — Name the alternate explanation strengthened by the missing sign.
rituals.win: ✓ What should have been there was missing—and that absence finally counted.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Name Explanation”; drop the scoreboard.
• If it flares, choose “Mark Absence”.
• “Mark Absence” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• At “Name Explanation”, compare “Ask Sign”.
• I can use “Search Fairly” without ranking my worth.
rituals.formula_flow: Ask Sign → Search Fairly → Mark Absence → Name Explanation
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
Never use absent evidence to dismiss subtle or delayed safety risks.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: THREE ACTIVE FUTURES ONLY
rituals.goal: Forecasts must compete for limited shelf space.
rituals.steps:
1. Picture Predictions — Picture the three predictions currently most relevant.
2. Enter Retiring — Any new prediction may enter only by retiring one, merging with one, or proving higher usefulness for a decision.
3. Cross Out — Remove retired entries from view.
4. Act Portfolio — Act from the remaining portfolio rather than unlimited mental possibilities.
rituals.win: ✓ Alarm lost its 100-percent certainty.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Act Portfolio”; drop the scoreboard.
• Restart detected: “Cross Out”.
• “Cross Out” keeps worth off scoreboards.
• Compare “Picture Predictions” with “Act Portfolio”.
• I can use “Enter Retiring” without ranking my worth.
rituals.formula_flow: Picture Predictions → Enter Retiring → Cross Out → Act Portfolio
rituals.safety:
PAUSE

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: VIVID IS NOT IMPORTANT
rituals.goal: Charge felt importance rent before it enters the decision.
rituals.steps:
1. Score Information — Score the information on two separate axes: how noticeable it feels and how much it changes the choice.
2. Pay Felt — A dramatic item with low relevance pays a felt importance tax and moves down the priority list.
3. Allocate Attention — Allocate attention to decision impact instead.
rituals.win: ✓ Made vividness pay rent before it could buy my attention.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Allocate Attention”; notice the room.
• Catch restart with “Pay Felt”.
• “Pay Felt” proves the present returned.
• Difference check: “Score Information” → “Allocate Attention”.
• I can use “Pay Felt” to return here.
rituals.formula_flow: Score Information → Pay Felt → Allocate Attention
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
High-felt importance warnings still deserve review when safety is plausible.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: STAMP THE ENDING INTO THE SENSES
rituals.goal: Useful reflection needs a finish signal physiology can recognise.
rituals.steps:
1. Choose A Finish — Choose one finish you can repeat: wash your hands, hear a soft sound, touch a doorframe, or change the light.
2. Pair It — Pair it with one short answer in your mind and a time to think about it again.
3. Close It — Use the sensory finish only when the topic is truly closed.
rituals.win: ✓ The topic got a sensory full stop instead of another mental reopening.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Close It”; notice the room.
• Skip replay; use “Pair It”.
• “Pair It” proves the present returned.
• “Choose A Finish” to “Close It”: what loosened?

rituals.formula_flow: Choose A Finish → Pair It → Close It
rituals.safety:

This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.

rituals.title: MEASURE THE EMOTION’S VELOCITY
rituals.goal: Intensity is a photograph; momentum is the film.
rituals.steps:
1. Set Level — At three intervals, keep not only level but direction and speed: rising fast, steady, falling slowly.
2. Add Action — Add the action impulse at each point.
3. Make Decisions — Make decisions from trajectory plus facts, not from the first intensity number alone.
rituals.win: ✓ The feeling became a moving trend, not a frozen number.
rituals.supports:
• Exhale after “Make Decisions”; let wanting crest.
• Loop back? Use “Add Action”.
• “Add Action” keeps wanting off controls.
• “Set Level” versus “Make Decisions”: what eased?
• I can use “Add Action” without obeying the urge.
rituals.formula_flow: Set Level → Add Action → Make Decisions
rituals.safety:
PAUSE
